title: The frontend lets a notification be deleted from the dashboard — a submitted one as readily as a draft — and DR1 defines no delete anywhere.

finding.frontend: Every row on the frontend dashboard carries a Delete link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-68). It opens a page of its own headed "Delete this notification?" whose only body text is "This cannot be undone.", offering a red "Yes, delete notification" button and a "No, return to dashboard" button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/copy/copy.en.js:1-6). The action is not limited to drafts: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/delete-notification/controller.js:19-22 admits draft, submitted and amending notifications alike, so a notification the authority has already received can be removed from the user's dashboard with one confirmation and no explanation of what that means. Underneath, the record is soft-deleted rather than destroyed, which the page's "This cannot be undone." does not tell the user.
finding.prototype: DR1's dashboard row offers two actions and neither is delete: "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262). No DR1 root view, route or link mentions deleting a notification, and the only delete-notification page in the prototype checkout sits under the design-release-2 and design-release-2.1 subtrees, which are later releases and not on trial here. DR1 is not squeamish about deletion in general: its address book gives a saved address a red Delete button on its own view page (app/views/address-book-view.html:43-46). It simply never applies the idea to a notification.
finding.difference: This is a capability the implementation has and the signed-off design does not describe, so there is nothing to bring the frontend into line with and nothing here for a developer to pick up yet. It needs a designer's ruling, and the ruling has to answer three things rather than one: whether a user may delete a notification at all; if so, whether that includes one already submitted to the authority or drafts only; and what the confirmation should say, because "This cannot be undone." is both the whole of the current explanation and not quite true of a soft delete. Until that is answered the finding cannot be settled either way. Nothing in the evidence can settle it — DR1's silence is equally consistent with delete being out of scope and with it having been overlooked.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a delete action, a delete confirmation, or any mention of removing a notification reachable from a DR1 session — a control on a root view, or a route that renders rather than redirects when the session is not a design-release-2 one.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs and both screenshots, and followed the delete through the source on both sides. The claim this slice rests on — that the frontend's delete is not limited to drafts — holds and I checked it twice: delete-notification/controller.js:19-22 defines deletable as DRAFT or SUBMITTED or AMEND, and the POST handler re-checks the same predicate at :44 before calling softDeleteJourney, so there is no second gate that quietly excludes a submitted notification. dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:25-28 builds one deleteAction and attaches it to all three status branches at :40, :50 and :64. The confirmation page is verbatim as described: fe-delete-notification.html:115 "Delete this notification?", :116 "This cannot be undone.", :121-122 a govuk-button--warning "Yes, delete notification", :125 "No, return to dashboard". The soft-delete claim holds on both adapters — real posts to a /soft-delete endpoint (services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/transition.js:44-49) and the stub sets the record to DELETED and filters it out of the list (services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:22-24) — so the record survives a confirmation that says it cannot be undone. On the DR1 side, dr1-dashboard.html:707-709 and dr1-dashboard-after-submission.html:707-709 offer Copy as new and View and nothing else. Ran the falsifier: see correction — it fires on the letter and not on the substance. Band disputed upheld.
finding.correction: The finding survives and the slots are left alone, but its falsifier is written loosely enough to fire on something that does not falsify it, which would cost the next reader an hour. It says any DR1 "route" mentioning deletion would settle it, and there is one: app/routes.js:10044 mounts GET /notifications/delete on the prototype's root router, with a POST beside it at :10048. Neither is reachable from DR1. renderDeleteNotificationPage (app/routes.js:5607-5613) redirects straight back to the dashboard unless isDesignRelease2SessionData(req.session.data), and the dashboard rows only carry a deleteHref when that same predicate is true (app/routes.js:6621-6623 and :6682-6684), so a DR1 session is never given the link and would be bounced if it typed the path. The falsifier has been narrowed to say that. One point in the finding's own reasoning is worth naming plainly, because it separates this finding from its sibling: DR1 does not contradict itself about delete the way it does about amend. It is simply silent, and the finding says so. That silence is why disputed is the honest band — DR1's address book proves the service is willing to delete things (app/views/address-book-view.html:43-46 gives a saved address a govuk-button--warning Delete), so the omission on notifications reads as a decision nobody wrote down rather than an oversight anyone can settle from the evidence.

relatedTo.why: the same designer's ruling covers both — what a user may do to a notification the authority has already received
